LVKE.|191}}</noinclude>him self: God, I giue thee thankes that I am not as the rest of men, extorcioners, vniust, aduouterers, as also this Publicane. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ To take pride of fasting, tithing, or any good worke, is naught: though the workes thē selues be very good.}}∷ I fast twise in a vveeke: I giue tithes of al that I possesse. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=13}}† And the Publicane standing a farre of vvould not so much as lift vp his eies tovvard heauen: but he {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ So doe the priests and people at the holy Altar knocke their breasts, & say with the humble Publicane, ''Deus propitius. August. ps. 31 conc, 3''.}}∷ knocked his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=14}}† I say to you, this man vvent dovvne into his house iustified more then he: because euery one that exalteth him self, shal be humbled: and he that humbleth him self, shal be exalted.⊣

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 13. Mr. 10, 13.''}}* And they brought vnto him infants also, that he might touche them. Vvhich thing vvhen the Disciples savv, they rebuked them. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=16}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} calling them together, said, Suffer children to come vnto me, and forbid them not, for the kingdom of heauen is for such. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=17}}† Amen I say to you, Whosoeuer receiueth not the kingdom of God {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ In matters of faith & religion we must be as humble & obedient to the Catholike Church as yong children to their parents.}}∷ as a childe, shal not enter into it.

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 16. Mr. 10, 17.''}}* And a certaine Prince asked him, saying, Good maister, by doing what, shal I possesse euerlasting life? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=19}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Vvhy doest thou call me good? None is good but only God. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=20}}† Thou knovvest {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 13.''}}* the commaundements: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not faith only but also keeping the commaundements purchase life euerlasting. See annot. Mat. ''19, 16''.}}∷ ''Thou shalt not kil, Thou shalt not commit aduoutrie, Thou shalt not beare false vvitnes, Thou shalt not steale, Honour thy father and mother''. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=21}}† Vvho said, Al these things haue I kept from my youth. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=22}}† Which {{sc|Iesvs}} hearing, said to him, Yet one thing thou lackest: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This is not a commaundment or precept, but counsel: which the religious do folow. See Annot. ''Mat. 19''.}}∷ Sel al that euer thou hast, and giue to the poore, and thou shalt haue treasure in heauen: and come, folovv me. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=23}}† He hearing these things, vvas stroken sad: because he vvas very riche. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=24}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} seeing him stroken sad, said, Hovv hardly shal they that haue money, enter into the kingdom of God? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=25}}† For it is easier for a camel to passe through the eie of a nedle, then for a riche man to enter into the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=26}}† And they that heard, said, And vvho can be saued? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=27}}† He said to them, The things that are impossible vvith men, are possible vvith God. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=28}}† And Peter said, Loe, vve haue left al things, and haue folowed thee. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=29}}† Vvho said to them, Amen I say to you, There is no man that hath leaft house, or parents, or brethren, or {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Apostles among other things left their wiues also, as S. Hierom noteth out of this place. ''li. 1 adu. Iouin''.}}∷ vvife, or children for the kingdom of God, {{verse|chapter=18|verse=30}}† and shal not receiue much more in this time, and in the world to come {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Life euerlasting the reward for leauing or losing willingly our goods for Christs sake.}}∷ life euerlasting.

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=31}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 17. Mr. 10, 32.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the Sunday of Quĩquagesme.}}And {{sc|Iesvs}} tooke the Tvvelue, and said to them, Behold vve goe vp to Hierusalem, and al things shal be<noinclude>{{rh|||consummate}}</noinclude>
